page: Amazon Web Services m5n.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server offering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on remote network-attached block volumes and Nitro hypervisor infrastructure. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Performance evaluations show strong multi-core computational throughput, highlighted by high scores in multi-core stress-ng tests and the PassMark CPU suite, including encryption and extended instruction benchmarks using AVX-512 vector extensions. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth tests also rank within the top 25 percent, supporting high-throughput operations such as Redis SET workloads at 74.81 million operations per second. However, single-core execution tests, such as single-core stress-ng and gzip compression, register in the lower quartile, and lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits text-generation performance on large language models.

From a resource perspective, the instance provides high compute density, memory bandwidth, and 100 Gbps networking. These characteristics make m5n.24xlarge suitable for distributed microservices, static web serving clusters, large-scale in-memory caching tiers, multi-threaded batch data processing, and enterprise application deployments requiring elevated network throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual machine configured with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The instance supplies 384.0 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, coupled with a 100 Gbps baseline network throughput. It features no local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect top-tier multi-threaded processing power, strong vector instruction execution via AVX-512, and high uncached memory bandwidth, driving 74.81 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-thread performance is modest, landing in the bottom quartile for single-core stress-ng tests, and generative AI execution is restricted by the absence of GPUs. Given its high core count, significant RAM, and massive network capacity, this instance fits high-throughput distributed applications, in-memory caching systems, data batch processing, and network-intensive enterprise workloads.
